claims.text: A homogenized CoCrFeMnNi HEA can have a single-phase FCC structure.
The homogenized single-phase alloy represents the current state of the art for structural HEAs.
Controlled aging after homogenization will nucleate and grow coherent L12-type or similar ordered nanoscale precipitates.
The proposed aging treatment will produce an ultrafine-grained matrix.
The resulting coherent nanoscale precipitates will be uniformly distributed within the matrix.
Coherent nanoscale precipitates impede dislocation glide and thereby increase strength.
Precipitate coherency minimizes stress concentrations that would otherwise reduce ductility.
Precipitate coherency minimizes stress concentrations that could reduce Young's modulus.
An ultrafine-grained matrix deflects or hinders cracks and thereby improves toughness.
The aged alloy will have higher yield strength than the unaged homogenized baseline.
The aged alloy will have greater ductility than the unaged homogenized baseline.
The aged alloy will have a higher Young's modulus than the unaged homogenized baseline.
The aged alloy will have greater fracture resistance than the unaged homogenized baseline.
Aging below the homogenization temperature can enable precipitation without excessive grain growth or brittle-phase formation.
The hypothesis requires sufficient phase stability and diffusion kinetics for controlled precipitation.
Precipitate overgrowth, unwanted secondary phases, or significant grain coarsening can prevent the predicted property improvements.
Failure to obtain statistically significant simultaneous improvements in all four measured properties is the specified falsification criterion.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says aging produces an ultrafine-grained matrix, but the stated intervention only ages an already homogenized alloy and includes no grain-refinement step; the conditions are instead designed to avoid grain growth. Thus, the origin of the ultrafine grains is internally unresolved.
